chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'd ibn Bakr from Habib al-Kha'thami from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him say: 'When a man sits for the Tashahhud and praises God, that suffices for him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The reason in this report is taqiyyah (concealment/prudence), because it is the view of the general public (Sunni), and we have clarified the obligation of the two testimonies of faith and the prayer upon Muhammad and his family.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: The sitting portion of prayer where testimonies and blessings are recited
key_terms.اَلتَّقِيَّةُ: Taqiyyah; prudence or concealment of religious rulings to avoid conflict or align with general practice
key_terms.مَذْهَبُ اَلْعَامَّةِ: The view/practice of the general public (Sunni)

ai.seo_question: Is reciting the full Tashahhud obligatory in Shia prayer or is praising God sufficient?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the principle of *taqiyyah* (prudence) in legal rulings, where the minimal act of praising God is deemed sufficient to align with the Sunni majority, despite the Shia position that reciting the two testimonies and sending blessings (*Salawat*) upon the Prophet and his family is obligatory. Shaykh al-Tusi records this in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to illustrate how jurists navigate between strict legal requirements and practical conformity in communal settings.
